channel.title: The ArmChair Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The ArmChair Journal (armchairjournal.com)

item.title: Western democracies on the edge? Polarisation, protests, and the battle for legitimacy - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Western democracies have been seeing a crisis of legitimacy as citizens are not trusting institutions and governments anymore. What would this lead to?

item.title: Neither Law nor Liberation: Maoism in Adivasi India - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Home Minister Amit Shah promised to eliminate Naxalism by 2026, the Communist Party of India (Maoist) appears to be in steep decline. Maoist jan adalats bypassed due process, while the state relied on exceptional legal regimes, vigilante formations like Salwa Judum, and expanded use of the UAPA.

item.title: Rebellious women: Whose JNU after all? - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: As the women of JNU who drove the university’s reputation and success over the years, they now face a twofold adversity: from the internal administration and from the external forces of society, all directed towards JNU. They face this because, first, they are women; second, because they are women of JNU.

item.title: Power, Poetry, and Protest: Churchill, Tagore, and Gandhi in the Early Twentieth Century - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Each of them shaped the politics of their times and continue to stay relevant even today. Comparing and contrasting Tagore, Churchill and Gandhi!

item.title: Sacred Stereotypes: How AI turns Faith into Fear - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Usage of AI to scale religious propaganda is exaggerated through fabricating evidence by AI-generated videos and photographs. This if further affected by lack of responsiveness of companies to take down hateful content on their platforms.

item.title: Cultural Invasion of Bengal: Hindutva challenge and the Left’s legacy - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: As BJP’s Hindutva project targets Bengal’s syncretic, Left-influenced political culture, the 2026 Assembly Elections become a battle over Bengali identity itself.

item.title: Shakti in Bengal politics: Durga Puja, Nationalism, and Sacred Power - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Explore how Shakti traditions, Durga Puja, and tantric culture shape political identity and state power in Bengal, from Bankim Chandra to contemporary leadership.

item.title: TMC’s Maa, Mati, Manush 2.0: From ‘Safeguarding’ to ‘Strategic state-building’ - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Explore how TMC’s 2026 manifesto shifts from welfare politics to long-term state-building, with promises on trade hubs, new districts, self-reliance, jobs, housing, and healthcare in West Bengal.

item.title: “We Are Indians Too”: From the North east - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: Colonial categorisation, state power, media narratives, and casual prejudice combine to marginalise people from India’s North east—and this must change.

item.title: Delimitation: The great Indian political surgery - The ArmChair Journal
item.description: The north-south debate needs a more holistic approach to address the delimitation exercise in India

item.title: Free-riders of Freedom: Political parties
item.description: Cash transfers are on the rise in India, compromising capital expenditures. Using game theory, political parties can be modelled in an externalities problem.

item.title: Sino-Taiwan tensions and India’s strategic dilemma
item.description: One-fifth of global maritime trade goes through Taiwan Strait. Amidst One China Policy and unofficial relations with Taiwan, India must ensure its tech supply chains are secure.

item.title: Coaching Classrooms, Or what do you call a group of parrots?
item.description: Under the lure of a good life, coaching centres in India exploit the dreams of parents and put students into cages that can’t dream

item.title: Learning in an Unfamiliar Tongue? Reflections from a Delhi School
item.description: Most Indian schools have children who have different mother-tongues compared to medium of instruction posing unique learning challenges to policymakers.

item.title: Great power rush in melting Arctic: Where does India stand?
item.description: Melting ice in the arctic and possibilities of energy resources has led to the US, Russia and China recalibrating their arctic positing. India must play a role too.
